title: The canonical diagonal torus in SL2
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Use the special linear group scheme $S=\mathrm{SL}_{2,k}$ of [def-sc-general-linear-group] and the multiplicative group $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ of [def-sc-gm-ga]. The diagonal torus inclusion $d:\mathbf G_{m,k}\to S$ is the scheme morphism dual to the $k$-algebra map $k[x_{11},x_{12},x_{21},x_{22}]/(x_{11}x_{22}-x_{12}x_{21}-1)\to k[t,t^{-1}]$ sending the four entries to $t,0,0,t^{-1}$ respectively. The determinant relation maps to zero because $tt^{-1}=1$. Thus on every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, its image consists precisely of $\operatorname{diag}(s,s^{-1})$ for $s\in R^\times$, including nonreduced $R$.
